message.content:
There's no pre-built binary. Let me think about this more carefully. The crash is a use-of-uninitialized-value. The fix commit `436143898` says the issue is that MSan doesn't see the inline asm writes to `z[8]` in `bigint_cnd_add/sub`. So the uninitialized read is in `bigint_cnd_add`/`bigint_cnd_sub` where `z[j]` is read after being written by inline asm.

But the crash state shows `bigint_cnd_abs`. Let me look more carefully. Maybe the crash state is just showing the top 3 frames and the actual issue is in `bigint_cnd_add`/`bigint_cnd_sub`. Actually, the crash state format in OSS-Fuzz shows the stack frames. Let me reconsider — maybe `bigint_cnd_abs` also has an issue.

Actually, wait. Let me re-read `bigint_cnd_abs`:
```cpp
void bigint_cnd_abs(word cnd, word x[], size_t size)
   {
   const word mask = CT::expand_mask(cnd);

   word carry = mask & 1;
   for(size_t i = 0; i != size; ++i)
      {
      const word z = word_add(~x[i], 0, &carry);
      x[i] = CT::select(mask, z, x[i]);
      }
   }
```

This reads `x[i]` for all `i < size`. If `x` = `a_w` and `a` was grown to `mod_words`, all words are initialized. So this shouldn't be the issue.

Hmm, but the crash state clearly shows `bigint_cnd_abs`. Let me reconsider. Maybe the issue is that `a` is `n` (the input), and `n` could be 0. When `n == 0`, `a` has 0 words. `a.grow_to(mod_words)` — but wait, does `grow_to` actually work when `a` is 0? Let me trace through:

`a = n` where `n == 0`. `a.grow_to(mod_words)`:
- `if(mod_words > size())` — `size()` = `m_reg.size()`. For a zero BigInt, `m_reg.size()` is 0. So `mod_words > 0` is true.
- `if(mod_words <= m_reg.capacity())` — if capacity >= mod_words, `m_reg.resize(m_reg.capacity())`. This resizes to capacity. New elements zero-initialized.

So `a_w` has `mod_words` (or more) initialized words. Fine.

OK let me think about this differently. Maybe the crash is actually in `bigint_cnd_add`/`bigint_cnd_sub` and the crash state is showing a different call path. Actually, let me look at the actual OSS-Fuzz testcase. The testcase ID is 5113093358092288. Let me try to download it.

Actually, let me reconsider. The crash state shows:
```
Botan::word_add
Botan::bigint_cnd_abs
Botan::ct_inverse_mod_odd_modulus
```

`word_add` is called from `bigint_cnd_abs`. In `bigint_cnd_abs`, `word_add(~x[i], 0, &carry)` reads `x[i]`. So `x[i]` = `a_w[i]` is uninitialized.

Wait — maybe the issue is that `a` is `n`, and `n` could be 0. When `n == 0`, `a.grow_to(mod_words)` grows `a` to `mod_words`. But then in the loop, `bigint_cnd_sub(odd_a, a_w.data(), b_w.data(), mod_words)` is called. `odd_a = a_w[0] & 1 = 0`. So no subtraction. Then `bigint_cnd_abs(0, a_w.data(), mod_words)` — `mask = 0`, so `CT::select(0, z, x[i])` returns `x[i]`. But `word_add(~x[i], 0, &carry)` still reads `x[i]`. If `x[i]` is uninitialized...

But we said `a` was grown to `mod_words` with zero-init. So `x[i]` is initialized.

Hmm, unless `grow_to` doesn't zero-initialize. Let me check `secure_vector`:
